vuln_id: ARVO arvo:63186 / bind9 add_link empty-chain duplicate check

classification.classification_note: The attacker controls the SIG(0) signer name that is looked up and the fact that the harness supplies a non-NULL view. The crashing `-1` subscript is created internally when `add_link()` performs its duplicate check on an empty `dns_qpchain_t`.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where the chain length is not checked to be nonzero before examining the last entry in add_link(). It is possible to reach add_link() without visiting an intermediate node first, and the check for a duplicate entry can then cause a crash.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 23-byte witness drives the `dns_message_checksig` fuzzer. Its first byte is `0x91`, so the harness builds a synthetic DNS message with a SIG(0) additional record and later calls `dns_message_checksig()` with a non-NULL `view`. `create_message()` copies the remaining 21 bytes verbatim as the SIG(0) RDATA, and `fromwire_sig()` parses the signer name `siG0key.` from those attacker-controlled bytes. `getsection()` appends that parsed RDATA to an `rdataset` and stores it as `msg->sig0`. `dns_message_checksig()` reparses `msg->sig0` into `dns_rdata_sig_t sig` and looks up `sig.signer` as a KEY record in the view's zone table. `dns_zt_find()` passes a caller-owned `dns_qpchain_t` into `dns_qp_lookup()`; `dns_qpchain_init()` zero-initializes `chain->len`, and the lookup later reaches the final `add_link(chain, n, offset)` branch while `chain->len` is still 0. `add_link()` immediately evaluates `chain->chain[chain->len - 1].node` as a duplicate-suppression check without first checking `chain->len != 0`. With `chain->len == 0`, the subscript expression becomes `-1`, and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reports `index -1 out of bounds` at `lib/dns/qp.c:2000`. The staged patch fixes this exact missing obligation by guarding the duplicate check with `chain->len != 0`.

source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path that consumes attacker-controlled SIG(0) signer bytes and materializes the lookup name later used by `dns_message_checksig()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 23-byte input `91 20 00 00 20 07 73 69 47 30 6b 65 79 00 20 20 20 20 20 20 c0 1f 20`. The harness copies bytes 2..22 into the synthetic SIG(0) RDATA. Within that RDATA, the final `c0 1f` pointer resolves to the earlier `07 73 69 47 30 6b 65 79 00` sequence, so this statement parses the signer name `siG0key.` from attacker-controlled bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement converts the attacker-controlled signer name into the qptrie search key bytes and length used by later `qpkey_compare()` and by the branch that reaches the crashing `add_link()` call.
tainted_value_origin.note: The signer name is materialized at source step 1, stored as `msg->sig0` at step 3, and reparsed as `sig.signer` at step 5. Here it becomes the internal trie key that drives the lookup path.

root_cause.description: The duplicate-suppression check dereferences the previous chain entry without first checking that the chain is non-empty.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact line to `if (chain->len != 0 && chain->chain[chain->len - 1].node == node) {`, adding the missing non-zero-length guard.

sink.description: UBSan sink. With `chain->len == 0`, this subscript reads `chain->chain[-1].node` before the first valid element of the 128-entry `chain[]` array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `qp.c:2000:6: runtime error: index -1 out of bounds for type 'struct (unnamed struct at ./include/dns/qp.h:247:2)[128]'` in `add_link` at this expression.

parser_admitted.description: The synthetic message has passed header and section parsing far enough that the additional record is accepted as SIG(0) and saved on the message object. Without this point, `dns_message_checksig()` would never enter the SIG(0) verification lookup path.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false and the reviewer feedback also leaves `needs_runtime_disambiguation` false, so Stage 02 stayed source-grounded and did not add marker instrumentation. The fact that the leaf-link call at `lib/dns/qp.c:2168` reaches `add_link()` with `chain->len` still zero is derived from the saved UBSan `index -1` crash plus the vulnerable source showing that `dns_qpchain_init()` zeroes `len` and that `add_link()` is the increment site before the crash line.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` adds the exact missing `chain->len != 0` guard at the crashing line.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged 23-byte witness makes the harness build a synthetic DNS message with a SIG(0) additional record and a non-NULL `view`; the parser materializes the attacker-chosen signer and stores the SIG(0) rdataset as `msg->sig0`.
SIG(0) verification reparses `msg->sig0` into `dns_rdata_sig_t sig`, materializes `sig.signer`, and uses that attacker-controlled name as a KEY lookup in the view's zone table.
The zone-table lookup forwards `sig.signer` into the qptrie, initializes the caller-owned chain with `len == 0`, and takes the final leaf-link branch that reaches `add_link()`.

The duplicate-suppression check reads the previous chain entry without a non-empty-chain guard. Because `chain->len` is still zero, `chain->chain[chain->len - 1]` becomes `chain[-1]` and UBSan reports index-out-of-bounds.

fine_trace.note: Source. The SIG(0) parser consumes the attacker-controlled signer field and appends its canonical name encoding to the RDATA buffer being built. For the staged witness, this parses signer `siG0key.`.
The parsed `rdata` object carrying those signer bytes is inserted into the SIG(0) rdataset, so the signer-bearing RDATA now lives in `rdataset` rather than only in parser locals.
Because this additional-section record is classified as SIG(0), the parser saves that rdataset on the message object. This is the exact stored RDATA later reparsed by `dns_message_checksig()`.
SIG(0) verification pulls the current `rdata` record back out of the saved `msg->sig0` rdataset, recovering the signer-bearing bytes stored at step 3.
`dns_rdata_tostruct()` interprets that stored SIG(0) RDATA as `dns_rdata_sig_t` and materializes `sig.signer` as the attacker-chosen lookup name `siG0key.`.
The witness supplies a non-NULL `view`, so the `view == NULL` guard is not taken and `dns_message_checksig()` starts a KEY lookup for `sig.signer` in the view's zone table.

fine_trace.code: result = dns_qp_lookup(&qpr, name, NULL, NULL, &chain, &pval, NULL);
fine_trace.note: The zone-table lookup forwards the attacker-controlled signer name into `dns_qp_lookup()` and supplies a real caller-owned `dns_qpchain_t chain` that the qptrie code will initialize and later append to.
`dns_qp_lookup()` converts that signer name into the internal qptrie key bytes and length that drive the later comparison and leaf-link branch.
This execution does not use the local fallback `oc`; `dns_qp_lookup()` invokes `dns_qpchain_init()` on the caller-supplied `chain` from step 7 before any trie links are added.
The compound literal zero-initializes unspecified fields of the caller-supplied chain, so `chain->len` becomes 0 and there is no valid previous `chain->chain[]` entry yet.
After descending to a leaf, the lookup compares the derived search key with the leaf key and computes `offset`, the value tested by the final exact/ancestor-match branch.
This branch is taken, so the lookup reaches the final leaf-link append at `add_link(chain, n, offset)` instead of falling through to the later ancestor-walk cleanup path.

Root cause. `add_link()` performs its duplicate-suppression check without first requiring `chain->len != 0`. The chain still has the zero value written at step 10, so this duplicate check has no previous entry to inspect.
With `chain->len == 0`, the subscript expression is formed as `0 - 1`. After the `uint8_t len` field is integer-promoted in this expression, the effective index is `-1`.

Sink. Using that underflowed index reads `chain->chain[-1].node` before the first valid element of the `chain[DNS_NAME_MAXLABELS]` array in `dns_qpchain_t`, producing the witnessed UBSan `index -1 out of bounds` report.

poc.trigger: /bin/arvo run in the vulnerable ARVO image executes /out/dns_message_checksig_fuzzer on /tmp/poc and reproduces UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: index -1 out of bounds in add_link.

format.name: 23-byte dns_message_checksig fuzzer input
format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact 23-byte input `91 20 00 00 20 07 73 69 47 30 6b 65 79 00 20 20 20 20 20 20 c0 1f 20`. Byte 0 is `0x91`, whose relevant crashing-path effect is `addasig=1`, `addtsig=0`, and `withview=1`, so the harness creates a SIG(0) additional record and later supplies a non-NULL `view` to `dns_message_checksig()`. `create_message()` copies the remaining 21 bytes verbatim as the SIG(0) RDATA. Within that RDATA, the signer name is encoded by the final `c0 1f` pointer to the earlier `07 73 69 47 30 6b 65 79 00` bytes, yielding `siG0key.`. The verified trigger semantics are exactly that this parsed SIG(0) signer reaches the qptrie KEY lookup, the final `add_link()` is the first link on that lookup, and `chain->chain[chain->len - 1]` is therefore evaluated with `chain->len == 0`.
